title: Incretin-based drugs and risk of intestinal obstruction among patients with type 2 diabetes
authors: Faillie JL, Yin H, Yu OHY, Herrero A, Altwegg R, Renoux C, et al.
population: New users of GLP-1 receptor agonists (25,617) against SGLT2 inhibitors (67,261) in the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink with linked hospital data; a second cohort compared DPP-4 inhibitors with SGLT2 inhibitors
funder: This study was funded by a Foundation Scheme grant (FDN-143328) from the Canadian Institutes of Health Research. No statement on funder role was given.
authorConflicts: One author served as a consultant for Janssen and Pfizer for work unrelated to this study; all other authors declared no competing interests.
result: Intestinal obstruction requiring hospitalisation occurred at 1.9 per 1000 person-years with GLP-1 receptor agonists against 1.1 with SGLT2 inhibitors (hazard ratio 1.69, 95% CI 1.04 to 2.74), highest after 1.6 years of use (3.48, 1.79 to 6.79); number needed to harm after 1 year 1223. DPP-4 inhibitors: 2.7 against 1.0 per 1000 person-years (2.59, 1.52 to 4.42). Semaglutide users generated no events; with the outcome restricted to the diagnostic codes most related to intestinal obstruction, GLP-1 receptor agonists were no longer associated with it.
